simple_definition: A machine that follows instructions to take in, change, keep and show information.
technical_definition: A programmable electronic device that executes stored instructions to process data received as input, retain results in storage and present output.
example: A laptop, a phone, a cash machine.

simple_definition: The physical parts of a computer.
technical_definition: The tangible components of a computing system, such as the processor, memory, storage devices, display and network adapter.

simple_definition: The part that carries out instructions.
technical_definition: The central processing unit: the hardware component that executes program instructions.
example: The chip that runs your browser's instructions.

simple_definition: Fast, temporary working space that is emptied when the power goes off.
technical_definition: Random-access memory: volatile, fast storage used for the data and instructions a computer is currently using.
example: The words you have typed but not yet saved.

simple_definition: Slower, permanent space that keeps information when the power is off.
technical_definition: Non-volatile data storage, such as a solid-state drive or hard disk, that retains data without power.

simple_definition: A unit for measuring stored information; enough for one English letter.
technical_definition: A unit of digital information made of eight bits.
example: The word 'Hi' takes two bytes in simple text.

simple_definition: Instructions that tell hardware what to do.
technical_definition: Programs and data that direct the operation of hardware.

simple_definition: Software that does a specific job for a person.
technical_definition: A program designed to perform a task for a user, running on top of an operating system.
example: A text editor, a browser, Git.

simple_definition: The main software that manages the computer, its files and the other programs.
technical_definition: System software that manages hardware resources, provides services such as file storage and process scheduling, and hosts applications.

simple_definition: A file or program that puts an application on your computer.
technical_definition: A program or package that copies an application's files to the correct locations and registers it with the operating system.
example: A Git setup file downloaded from the maker's site.

simple_definition: An account or permission level allowed to change the computer's system settings.
technical_definition: A privileged user role that may modify system-wide configuration and install software for all users.
example: The prompt that asks whether to allow an installer to make changes.

simple_definition: A program that installs and updates applications from a trusted collection.
technical_definition: A tool that resolves, retrieves, installs, updates and removes software packages from configured repositories.

simple_definition: A named collection of information kept in storage.
technical_definition: A named sequence of bytes stored in a file system, with associated metadata.

simple_definition: Information about a file, such as its size, dates, owner and permissions.
technical_definition: Attributes a file system records about a file separately from the file's contents.
example: The size and last-changed date shown in a detailed listing.

simple_definition: The letters after the last dot in a file name; a label for the kind of contents.
technical_definition: A suffix of a file name, conventionally indicating the file's format; it does not change the contents.

simple_definition: A container that holds files and other folders.
technical_definition: A file-system object that contains references to files and other directories.

simple_definition: The folder that belongs to your user account.
technical_definition: The directory assigned to a user account for that user's files and settings; often written ~ in a shell.

simple_definition: The top folder of a tree; everything else is inside it.
technical_definition: The topmost directory of a file-system hierarchy, written / on Unix-like systems.

simple_definition: A written description of where a file or folder is in the tree.
technical_definition: A sequence of directory names, separated by a separator character, identifying a location in a file system.

simple_definition: A path that starts at the root and means the same wherever you are.
technical_definition: A path that begins at the file-system root (or a drive letter on Windows) and fully specifies a location.

simple_definition: A path that starts from where you are now.
technical_definition: A path interpreted relative to the current working directory.

simple_definition: The folder that counts as 'here' when you give a relative path.
technical_definition: The directory against which a process resolves relative paths.
example: sunrise-bakery after you have moved into it.

simple_definition: A file that ordinary listings do not show unless asked.
technical_definition: A file whose name (on Unix-like systems, a leading dot) or attribute marks it to be omitted from default listings.

simple_definition: A rule about who may read, change or run a file.
technical_definition: An access-control attribute governing read, write and execute rights of users on a file or directory.

simple_definition: Information stored as ordinary characters with no fonts, colours or layout.
technical_definition: A sequence of encoded characters with no formatting metadata, stored as bytes according to a character encoding.

simple_definition: A file that is not plain text, such as a photo or a word-processor document.
technical_definition: A file whose bytes are not a sequence of characters intended to be read as text.

simple_definition: One file that holds other files in compressed form.
technical_definition: A container format that stores multiple files, optionally compressed, in a single file.
example: Many word-processor documents are ZIP archives internally.

simple_definition: A program for creating and changing plain text files.
technical_definition: An application that edits plain text without adding formatting information.
example: Any editor that saves only characters.
related: code editor; word processor; plain text

simple_definition: A program for writing formatted documents, saved in a packaged format.
technical_definition: An application that edits formatted documents, storing styles and layout along with the text, normally in a binary or packaged format.

simple_definition: A text editor with extra help for writing structured text such as software.
technical_definition: A text editor providing features such as syntax highlighting, line numbers, multi-file search and folder navigation.
example: An editor showing your project's files in a side panel.

simple_definition: Colouring parts of text according to their role so the structure is easy to see.
technical_definition: Display of tokens of structured text in different colours or styles according to their syntactic category.
example: Tags in HTML shown in one colour and words in another.

simple_definition: The folder of files that makes up one piece of work.
technical_definition: A set of files, typically under one directory, that together form a program, website, document set or tool.

simple_definition: The human-written files from which a project is made.
technical_definition: Human-readable files that specify a program, website or document set and from which deliverables are produced.

simple_definition: A text format that marks up web pages so a browser knows how to show them.
technical_definition: HyperText Markup Language: a markup language using tags to describe the structure of a web page.

simple_definition: A text format that describes how web pages look.
technical_definition: Cascading Style Sheets: a language for describing the presentation of documents written in a markup language.

simple_definition: A single unit of text: a letter, digit, symbol, emoji or space.
technical_definition: An abstract unit of written text identified by a Unicode code point.

simple_definition: The rule that turns characters into bytes and back.
technical_definition: A mapping between sequences of characters and sequences of bytes used to store or transmit text.

simple_definition: A universal list that gives every character a number.
technical_definition: A standard that assigns a unique code point to each character of the world's writing systems and many symbols.

simple_definition: The most widely used way to store Unicode text as bytes.
technical_definition: A variable-width encoding of Unicode that uses one to four bytes per character and is backward compatible with ASCII for basic English characters.
example: é is stored as the two bytes c3 a9.

simple_definition: Garbled text caused by reading with the wrong encoding.
technical_definition: Incorrect characters displayed when bytes are decoded using an encoding different from the one used to encode them.

simple_definition: The invisible character or characters that end a line of text.
technical_definition: A control character sequence marking a line break: LF on Unix-like systems, CRLF traditionally on Windows.

simple_definition: Computers connected so that they can exchange information.
technical_definition: A set of computing devices linked by communication channels.

simple_definition: The worldwide system of connected networks.
technical_definition: The global interconnection of networks that use common protocols to exchange data.
example: The connection between your laptop and a server in another country.

simple_definition: Linked pages and applications you view with a browser.
technical_definition: A system of interlinked resources, identified by URLs and transferred using HTTP, accessed with browsers over the internet.

simple_definition: An application for viewing web pages.
technical_definition: A client application that requests, interprets and displays web resources.
example: The program in which you open index.html.

simple_definition: The written address of a page or resource on the internet.
technical_definition: Uniform Resource Locator: a string that identifies a resource by scheme, host, optional port, path, optional query and optional fragment.

simple_definition: A human-friendly name, such as example.org, for a host on the internet.
technical_definition: A hierarchical name registered in the domain name system that resolves to network addresses.

simple_definition: A number that identifies a computer on a network.
technical_definition: A numeric identifier assigned to a network interface, used to route packets.

simple_definition: The internet's phone book: it turns names into numbers.
technical_definition: A distributed naming system that resolves domain names to IP addresses and other records.

simple_definition: The computer or program that asks for something.
technical_definition: The party in a client-server exchange that initiates requests.

simple_definition: A computer or program that answers requests.
technical_definition: A process (or the computer running it) that listens for and responds to requests from clients.
example: The program that sends you a web page.

simple_definition: The rules web clients and servers follow to exchange requests and replies.
technical_definition: HyperText Transfer Protocol: an application-layer protocol of requests and responses carrying methods, status codes, headers and bodies.

simple_definition: HTTP with encryption and a check of the server's identity.
technical_definition: HTTP carried over an encrypted, authenticated TLS connection.

simple_definition: On the computer you are using.
technical_definition: Residing on, or executing on, the machine at hand rather than reached over a network.
example: A file in your sharif-git-lab folder.

simple_definition: On a different computer, reached over a network.
technical_definition: Residing on another machine, accessed through a network connection.
example: A page on example.org; later, a repository on GitHub.

simple_definition: A record a service keeps to represent you.
technical_definition: A stored identity with credentials, settings and permissions maintained by a service.

simple_definition: The name that identifies your account.
technical_definition: A unique identifier for an account within a service.

simple_definition: A secret string you present to prove you own an account.
technical_definition: A memorised secret used as a credential in authentication.
example: A long passphrase of unrelated words.

simple_definition: An application that stores all your passwords securely and fills them in.
technical_definition: Software that keeps credentials in an encrypted vault protected by a master secret.
example: An app protected by one strong master password.

simple_definition: Proving who you are with two proofs from different families.
technical_definition: Authentication requiring two distinct factors: something known, something held, or something inherent.
example: Password plus a code from a phone app.

simple_definition: Proving who you are.
technical_definition: The process of verifying the identity claimed by a user or program.
example: Entering a password and a code.

simple_definition: Deciding what you are allowed to do once your identity is known.
technical_definition: The process of determining whether an authenticated identity may perform a requested action.
example: You can read a project but not delete it.

simple_definition: Giving only the access that is needed, and no more.
technical_definition: A design principle that grants a subject the minimum permissions required for its task.
example: A token that can read one project only.

simple_definition: A limited stand-in for a password; still a secret.
technical_definition: A credential string that grants specified, often time-limited, permissions to its holder.
example: A personal access token used by a tool.

simple_definition: A shareable public key and a private key that never leaves your computer.
technical_definition: A matched public/private cryptographic key pair in which data signed or locked with one key is verified or unlocked with the other.

simple_definition: A secure way to connect to another computer, which can use a key pair to prove your identity.
technical_definition: A cryptographic network protocol for secure remote login and command execution, supporting public-key authentication.
example: Connecting to a server without sending a password.

simple_definition: Tricking someone into giving away a secret by pretending to be trusted.
technical_definition: A social-engineering attack that impersonates a trusted party to obtain credentials or induce harmful actions.
example: An urgent email with a link to a lookalike site.

simple_definition: A window in which you type commands and read text replies.
technical_definition: A text-based interface (terminal emulator) through which a user interacts with a shell.
example: The Terminal application or Git Bash window.

simple_definition: The program that reads your commands and has them carried out.
technical_definition: A command interpreter that reads input, parses commands and asks the operating system to execute them.

simple_definition: One instruction typed to the shell.
technical_definition: A line of input consisting of a program name followed by options and arguments, executed by the shell.

simple_definition: The text the shell shows when it is waiting for you to type.
technical_definition: A string printed by the shell to indicate readiness for input.

simple_definition: A widely used shell; the one this book uses for its examples.
technical_definition: The Bourne-Again Shell, a Unix command interpreter.

simple_definition: A Bash environment for Windows that is installed with Git for Windows; it is not Git itself.
technical_definition: A terminal providing a Bash shell and Unix-style utilities on Windows, distributed with Git for Windows.
example: The window you open to type Git commands on Windows.

simple_definition: A word that changes how a command behaves.
technical_definition: A command-line parameter, usually prefixed with one or two dashes, that modifies a command's behaviour.

simple_definition: The thing a command acts on, such as a file name.
technical_definition: A value passed to a command on the command line.

simple_definition: A named piece of text the shell remembers.
technical_definition: A named storage location in a shell holding a string value that can be referenced in later commands.

simple_definition: A variable that programs started from the shell can read.
technical_definition: A variable exported into the environment inherited by child processes.

simple_definition: Prints the folder you are currently in.
technical_definition: Print working directory: outputs the absolute path of the current directory.

simple_definition: Creates a new folder.
technical_definition: Make directory: creates directories; -p also creates missing parent directories.

simple_definition: Moves you into another folder.
technical_definition: Change directory: sets the shell's current working directory.

simple_definition: Creates an empty file, or updates a file's last-changed time.
technical_definition: Creates an empty file if it does not exist, or updates its timestamps.

simple_definition: The list of folders the shell searches for programs.
technical_definition: An environment variable containing an ordered list of directories searched to resolve command names. Not to be confused with a file path.
example: A tool in a folder not on PATH gives 'command not found'.

simple_definition: A way of writing formatted text using plain-text marks.
technical_definition: A lightweight markup language whose plain-text syntax is converted to structured documents such as HTML.

simple_definition: A program that turns marked-up text into a formatted result.
technical_definition: Software that parses a markup language and produces a presentation, such as HTML, from it.

simple_definition: A precise written specification of the core Markdown syntax.
technical_definition: A standardised specification of Markdown syntax intended to make different implementations behave consistently.

simple_definition: A copy of your files kept elsewhere so they can be restored after loss.
technical_definition: A duplicate of data stored separately from the original to allow recovery after loss or damage.
example: A nightly copy of a laptop to an external drive.

simple_definition: A folder whose contents are kept the same across computers or an online service.
technical_definition: A directory whose contents are replicated automatically between devices or a service.
example: A folder that appears on your laptop and phone.

simple_definition: One particular state of a file or project at a point in time.
technical_definition: A distinct recorded state of a file or project.
example: The menu as it was on Monday.

simple_definition: The recorded sequence of versions of a project, with reasons and authors.
technical_definition: The ordered record of a project's versions together with metadata such as author, date and description.
example: Every recorded change to the bakery menu.

simple_definition: A system that records a project's history so changes can be seen, reversed and combined.
technical_definition: A system that records changes to files over time, supporting retrieval of earlier versions, comparison, and collaborative work.

simple_definition: A marker that stops others from changing a file until you release it.
technical_definition: A mechanism preventing concurrent modification of a resource by others.

simple_definition: To combine two sets of changes into one.
technical_definition: The operation of integrating changes from two lines of work into a single version.
example: Joining Alice's cake addition and Bob's price change.

simple_definition: A project together with the complete record of its history.
technical_definition: A store containing a project's files and the full history of changes to them; in Git, the project folder plus its .git directory.
example: The sunrise-bakery folder after Git is started in it.

simple_definition: One server holds the only complete history; users hold working copies.
technical_definition: A version-control architecture with a single central repository that clients connect to.
example: A shared server everyone must reach to record work.
related: distributed version control; single point of failure

simple_definition: Every user holds a complete copy of the repository and its history.
technical_definition: A version-control architecture in which each participant has a full repository, and repositories exchange history peer to peer.

simple_definition: A complete copy of a repository, with all its history, made on another computer.
technical_definition: A full copy of a repository including history, produced by cloning.
example: Your copy of a project from a shared server.

simple_definition: A part whose failure stops everything or loses something irreplaceable.
technical_definition: A component in a system whose failure causes the entire system to fail.
example: A single central server with no backup.

simple_definition: A free, open-source version-control system that runs on your computer.
technical_definition: A distributed version-control system that records the history of a project in a repository.
example: The program you use to record versions of sunrise-bakery.

simple_definition: An online service that stores shared repositories and adds collaboration features.
technical_definition: A web service providing remote repository storage and collaboration tools such as issue tracking and review.

simple_definition: A widely used online platform for hosting Git repositories and collaborating on software.
technical_definition: A hosting platform built around Git repositories with collaboration and automation features.

simple_definition: Another hosting platform for Git repositories.
technical_definition: A hosting platform for Git repositories with collaboration and automation features.

simple_definition: Another hosting platform for Git repositories, from a different company.
technical_definition: A hosting platform for Git repositories with collaboration features.
example: A team's repository hosted outside GitHub.

simple_definition: The command that reads and changes Git's settings.
technical_definition: Reads, writes and lists Git configuration values across system, global, local and worktree scopes.

simple_definition: A Git setting that applies to your user account in every repository.
technical_definition: A configuration value stored in the user's global file (~/.gitconfig) and applied to all repositories of that user.

simple_definition: A named value that changes how Git behaves.
technical_definition: A key of the form section.name with a value, read from Git's configuration files, environment and command line.

simple_definition: The level at which a setting is stored: system, global, local or worktree.
technical_definition: The configuration file level (system, global, local, worktree) at which a value is stored, determining its reach and precedence.
example: A local value beats a global one in that repository.

simple_definition: To replace a setting's value for one command or one shell.
technical_definition: To supply a value that takes precedence over stored configuration, for example with git -c or an environment variable.

simple_definition: A complete picture of all the files of a project at one moment.
technical_definition: The state of the tracked files at a point in time, as recorded by a commit's tree.
example: The whole bakery site as it was when you committed.

simple_definition: The folder of files you see and edit.
technical_definition: The checked-out files of a repository on disk, including changes not yet staged or committed.

simple_definition: The holding area that lists exactly what the next commit will contain.
technical_definition: Git's staging area (index): a file in .git recording the content that will form the next commit.

simple_definition: To add a file's current contents to the index so the next commit includes them.
technical_definition: To record a file's current state in the index (git add).

simple_definition: The complete history, kept in the hidden .git folder on your computer.
technical_definition: The .git directory holding a project's objects, references and configuration.

simple_definition: A file Git knows about, because it is in the last commit or in the index.
technical_definition: A file present in the index or in HEAD's tree.

simple_definition: A recorded snapshot with author, time, message and a link to the previous commit; also the action of making one.
technical_definition: A Git object recording a tree, parent commits, author and committer identities, timestamps and a message.

simple_definition: The long code that uniquely identifies a commit.
technical_definition: A cryptographic hash of an object's content, used as its identifier; usually abbreviated.

simple_definition: A movable name that points to a commit.
technical_definition: A reference under refs/heads that holds the identifier of a commit and moves forward with new commits.

simple_definition: The pointer that says which commit you are currently on.
technical_definition: A reference, normally symbolic, to the current branch or commit; the parent of the next commit.

simple_definition: Creates a new repository in the current folder.
technical_definition: Initialises an empty Git repository by creating the .git directory.

simple_definition: Shows which files are untracked, modified or staged, and the current branch.
technical_definition: Reports the state of the working tree and index relative to HEAD; read-only.

simple_definition: Stages files so they are part of the next commit.
technical_definition: Updates the index with the current content of the given paths.

simple_definition: Records the staged snapshot with a message.
technical_definition: Creates a commit object from the index and advances the current branch.

simple_definition: Shows the history of commits, newest first.
technical_definition: Lists commits reachable from the current revision in reverse chronological order, with options for format and filtering.

simple_definition: Any way of naming a commit: a hash, a branch name, HEAD, HEAD~2.
technical_definition: A specifier that resolves to a commit (or other object), as defined by Git's revision syntax.

simple_definition: A report of the differences between two versions, line by line.
technical_definition: A description of changes between two file or tree states, shown as removed (-) and added (+) lines in hunks.

simple_definition: One contiguous chunk of changes in a diff.
technical_definition: A group of adjacent changed lines with context in a unified diff, introduced by an @@ header.

simple_definition: Displays one commit: its message and changes.
technical_definition: Shows a commit's metadata and diff (or other objects).

simple_definition: A file Git has been told to leave alone.
technical_definition: A file matching an ignore pattern that Git omits from untracked listings and from git add of directories.

simple_definition: A text file listing patterns of files Git should ignore.
technical_definition: A file whose lines are patterns (with comments and negations) applied to paths under its directory; normally tracked.

simple_definition: Renames or moves a file and stages the change.
technical_definition: Moves a file in the working tree and index in one operation.

simple_definition: Deletes a file and stages the deletion.
technical_definition: Removes a path from the working tree and the index; with --cached only from the index.

simple_definition: Replaces the last commit with a new one, to fix its message or add forgotten changes.
technical_definition: Creates a new commit from the index and message that replaces the tip commit; the replaced commit is left unreferenced.

simple_definition: A commit containing one logical change.
technical_definition: A commit that is complete and self-contained, with a single purpose, that can be reviewed or reverted independently.

simple_definition: A commit with a message but no file change.
technical_definition: A commit whose tree is identical to its parent's, created with --allow-empty.
example: Mark the start of the spring menu

simple_definition: Lists, creates, renames and deletes branches.
technical_definition: Manages branch references under refs/heads.

simple_definition: Changes the current branch.
technical_definition: Moves HEAD to another branch and updates the index and working tree to match.

simple_definition: HEAD points directly at a commit instead of a branch.
technical_definition: A state in which HEAD contains a commit identifier rather than a symbolic reference to a branch.

simple_definition: A merge that only moves a branch pointer forward.
technical_definition: A merge in which the receiving branch has not diverged, so Git moves its pointer to the source commit and creates no merge commit.

simple_definition: Each branch has commits the other lacks.
technical_definition: Two branches have diverged when neither tip is an ancestor of the other, so a fast-forward is impossible.
example: Hours added on main while tea is added on add-tea.

simple_definition: A commit that joins two lines of work.
technical_definition: A commit with two or more parents, recording where lines of work were combined.

simple_definition: Turn many commits into one.
technical_definition: Combine the changes of several commits into a single new commit, leaving no link to the originals.

simple_definition: Git cannot combine two changes by itself.
technical_definition: A situation in which both sides changed the same part of a file differently, so Git stops the merge and asks the user to decide.
example: Two branches set the white loaf price differently.

simple_definition: The lines Git writes into a conflicted file.
technical_definition: The <<<<<<<, ======= and >>>>>>> lines that delimit the two versions; all must be removed before committing.

simple_definition: A repository with no working files, used as a shared hub.
technical_definition: A repository holding only Git's database, with no checked-out working tree; the form used for shared remotes.

simple_definition: Your note of where a remote branch was when you last looked.
technical_definition: A read-only local reference such as origin/main that Git updates on fetch, pull and push.

simple_definition: The remote branch a local branch follows.
technical_definition: The branch named by branch.<name>.remote and branch.<name>.merge, used by plain push, pull and status.

simple_definition: Download new commits without changing your branches.
technical_definition: Retrieve objects and update remote-tracking branches, leaving local branches and the working tree untouched.

simple_definition: Fetch, then merge into your current branch.
technical_definition: git fetch followed by integrating the upstream branch into the current branch, by default with a merge.

simple_definition: A shelf for unfinished changes.
technical_definition: A stack of saved working-tree and index states that lets you return to a clean tree and reapply the changes later.

simple_definition: A fixed name for one commit.
technical_definition: A reference that names a commit and, unlike a branch, does not move when new commits are made.

simple_definition: A tag that is just a name.
technical_definition: A tag that is only a reference to a commit, with no tagger, date or message of its own.

simple_definition: A tag with a message and tagger.
technical_definition: A tag stored as its own object with tagger, date and message; the usual choice for releases.

simple_definition: Bring a file back from the index or an older commit.
technical_definition: Restores content into the working tree or, with --staged, into the index, from the index or a named commit.

simple_definition: Move the current branch to another commit.
technical_definition: Moves the current branch to a commit; --soft keeps index and working tree, the default resets the index, --hard resets both.

simple_definition: Undo a commit by adding a new one.
technical_definition: Creates a new commit that applies the inverse of an earlier commit, leaving history intact.

simple_definition: Git's private diary of where HEAD has been.
technical_definition: A local, temporary log of the positions of HEAD and each branch, used to recover commits that are no longer reachable.

simple_definition: Replay your commits on top of another commit.
technical_definition: Reapply the commits of a branch, one by one, on a new base, producing new commits with new hashes.

simple_definition: Copy one commit onto another branch.
technical_definition: Apply the change introduced by an existing commit as a new commit on the current branch.

simple_definition: Find the commit that broke something by halving.
technical_definition: A binary search through history that repeatedly checks out the middle of the remaining range to find the first bad commit.

simple_definition: A text file that describes a change.
technical_definition: A text file describing changes to files so that they can be applied elsewhere, for example with git apply or git am.

simple_definition: A convention for MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH release numbers.
technical_definition: A versioning convention in which MAJOR changes for incompatible changes, MINOR for compatible additions and PATCH for compatible fixes; a hyphenated label marks a pre-release.

simple_definition: Any item in Git's database.
technical_definition: One of the four kinds of stored item in Git's object database: blob, tree, commit or tag, each named by a hash.

simple_definition: The stored contents of one file.
technical_definition: An object holding the contents of a single file, with no name, folder or date.

simple_definition: A stored list of a folder's contents.
technical_definition: An object listing the entries of one folder, each with a mode, type, hash and name.

simple_definition: A name that points to an object.
technical_definition: A named pointer, stored as a small file under .git/refs, holding a hash or another ref's name; branches and tags are refs.

simple_definition: The object an annotated tag creates.
technical_definition: An object naming another object with a type, tag name, tagger and message.

simple_definition: One file holding many objects compactly.
technical_definition: A file that stores many objects together, using differences between similar objects; created by git gc and by network transfers.

simple_definition: Git's housekeeping of stored objects.
technical_definition: git gc packs loose objects into packfiles and removes unreachable objects after a safety period.

simple_definition: A stored object nothing points to.
technical_definition: An object in the database that no ref leads to; removed by garbage collection eventually.

simple_definition: An extra working folder for the same repository.
technical_definition: An additional working directory linked to one repository, with its own checked-out branch and shared history.

simple_definition: A clone with only the recent history.
technical_definition: A clone limited to a given number of recent commits, with older history cut off (grafted) until fetched.

simple_definition: A repository pinned inside another repository.
technical_definition: A repository at a fixed path in another repository; the outer one records one commit of the inner one (mode 160000), described in .gitmodules.

simple_definition: A way to keep large files outside the history.
technical_definition: An extension that stores large file contents on a separate server and leaves small pointer files in the repository.

simple_definition: Your own short name for a Git command.
technical_definition: A name defined in configuration (alias.<name>) as a shortcut for another Git command, or for a shell command when it starts with !.

simple_definition: A script Git runs at a fixed moment.
technical_definition: A script in .git/hooks that Git runs at a specific moment, such as before a commit; a failing exit status stops the operation.

simple_definition: A program that remembers passwords for Git.
technical_definition: A program that Git asks to store, return or delete the username and password or token for a remote address.

simple_definition: Git remembers how you resolved a conflict.
technical_definition: A feature (reuse recorded resolution) that records a conflict resolution and applies it when the same conflict recurs.

simple_definition: A value that gives access if someone else has it.
technical_definition: A password, token, API key, private key or file containing them, which gives access to a system when held by someone else.

simple_definition: A commit that carries a verifiable signature.
technical_definition: A commit carrying a cryptographic signature made with the author's private key, which others can check against the public key.

simple_definition: The agreed way a team uses Git.
technical_definition: The agreed way a person or team uses branches, commits, reviews, merges and releases to get changes into a project.

simple_definition: The short line showing how to write a command.
technical_definition: The compact notation at the start of a command's usage or manual page that shows its options and arguments, with brackets for optional parts and angle brackets for placeholders.

simple_definition: A password-like secret for programs.
technical_definition: A secret string that a program presents instead of a password, which can be limited in permissions and lifetime and revoked separately.

simple_definition: A message from a platform that something happened where you are subscribed.
technical_definition: An update delivered to a notifications inbox, a mobile app or email because of activity in a conversation or repository to which a user is subscribed.
example: A message that someone commented on your pull request.

simple_definition: An arrangement to be told about activity in one conversation or repository.
technical_definition: A recorded preference that causes a platform to send notifications about a specific conversation or repository to a user until the user unsubscribes.
example: Commenting on an issue subscribes you to it.

simple_definition: A file that introduces a project to the people who arrive at it.
technical_definition: A documentation file, conventionally named README.md, placed at the root (or in a .github or docs folder) of a repository and displayed on its front page by hosting platforms.

simple_definition: A short label that helps people find a repository.
technical_definition: A lowercase label attached to a hosted repository to classify its purpose, subject area, community or language, and to enable search and browsing by that label.

simple_definition: A section of a repository for long documentation, kept as its own Git repository.
technical_definition: A documentation area attached to a hosted repository, stored as a separate Git repository (addressed with a .wiki.git suffix on GitHub) with its own history.

simple_definition: A numbered item where a problem, idea or task is written down and discussed.
technical_definition: A tracked item in a hosted repository with a title, description, discussion and open or closed state, identified by a number unique within the repository.

simple_definition: A form, defined in a file, that guides people to write a useful issue.
technical_definition: A YAML template stored under .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE that defines input fields whose values are converted into a Markdown issue.

simple_definition: A proposal to merge one branch into another, with a place to discuss it first.
technical_definition: A hosting-platform feature that records a request to merge a compare branch into a base branch and collects discussion, reviews and automated check results; it is not a Git object.
example: A pull request from add-tea into main.

simple_definition: The branch a pull request wants to change.
technical_definition: The branch into which the changes of a pull request are to be merged, usually the default branch.

simple_definition: The branch that holds the changes in a pull request.
technical_definition: The topic (head) branch of a pull request, whose commits are proposed for merging into the base branch.

simple_definition: Reading someone else's proposed change before it is merged.
technical_definition: The practice of examining a proposed change to detect defects, share knowledge and decide whether it is ready to be integrated.
example: A colleague comments on three lines of your pull request.

simple_definition: A table, board or roadmap for planning work across issues and pull requests.
technical_definition: A hosting-platform planning tool that presents issues, pull requests and draft items in table, board and roadmap layouts with custom fields, filters and automation.
example: A board with the columns Todo, In progress and Done.

simple_definition: A block of time in which a team plans to finish some work.
technical_definition: A repeating, fixed-length period of planned work; in GitHub Projects, a field type that groups items by such periods.

simple_definition: An open-ended conversation about a project, kept apart from the list of issues.
technical_definition: A hosting-platform forum thread, filed in a category, used for questions, ideas, announcements and polls that are not yet tracked work.
example: A Q&A thread asking how to install the tool.

simple_definition: Your own hosted copy of someone else's repository.
technical_definition: A copy of a hosted repository owned by another account, connected to the original (the upstream), used to propose changes back through pull requests without write access to the original.
example: Your copy of an open-source project on the platform.

simple_definition: A person or team responsible for reviewing changes to certain files.
technical_definition: A user or team named in a CODEOWNERS file who is automatically requested to review pull requests that change matching files.

simple_definition: A setting that protects chosen branches from risky changes.
technical_definition: A repository setting on a hosting platform that matches branch names by pattern and applies restrictions or requirements, such as required reviews and blocked force pushes.
example: A rule on main that requires one review.

simple_definition: A named list of rules that a platform enforces on branches or tags.
technical_definition: A set of rules applied by a hosting platform to selected branches or tags, layered with other rulesets so that the most restrictive version of each rule applies.
example: A ruleset that blocks force pushes to release branches.

simple_definition: Checking every change automatically as soon as it is committed.
technical_definition: The practice of frequently committing code to a shared repository and automatically building and testing each change to detect errors early.
example: A server runs the tests on every pull request.

simple_definition: Publishing software automatically after it passes its checks.
technical_definition: The practice of using automation to publish and deploy software updates, typically after the code has been built and tested automatically.
example: A merge to main publishes the website.

simple_definition: The ordered steps a change goes through automatically.
technical_definition: An ordered sequence of automated stages, such as lint, test, build and deploy, in which a failure normally stops later stages.

simple_definition: A readable text format for settings and lists, written with indentation.
technical_definition: A human-readable data-serialisation format that represents scalars, sequences and mappings using indentation (spaces only) and simple punctuation; used for configuration such as GitHub Actions workflows.

simple_definition: Something that happens in a repository and can start a workflow.
technical_definition: An activity in a repository, such as a push, pull request or issue, or a schedule or manual request, that triggers a workflow run.

simple_definition: A group of steps that run together on one machine.
technical_definition: A set of steps in a workflow executed on the same runner; jobs run in parallel unless one declares a dependency on another.

simple_definition: One task inside a job.
technical_definition: A single command (run) or action (uses) executed in order within a job, in its own process.

simple_definition: The machine that runs a job.
technical_definition: A virtual machine or container, hosted by the platform or by the user, that executes the jobs of a workflow.

simple_definition: A reusable piece of code that a step can use.
technical_definition: A predefined, reusable unit of code used in a workflow step to perform a task such as checking out a repository or setting up a toolchain.

simple_definition: An automated process defined in a file in the repository.
technical_definition: A configurable automated process defined by a YAML file in .github/workflows that runs one or more jobs when triggered by an event.

simple_definition: A small formula in a workflow that GitHub works out while running.
technical_definition: A construct written between ${{ and }} in a workflow file that GitHub evaluates using literals, operators, functions and contexts.

simple_definition: A collection of information that a workflow can read.
technical_definition: A named object, such as github, env, steps or runner, whose properties can be read in workflow expressions.

simple_definition: A file a workflow produces and keeps.
technical_definition: A file or collection of files produced during a workflow run and stored so that it persists after the job and can be shared with other jobs.
example: A built program or a test report.

simple_definition: A way to run the same job in several configurations.
technical_definition: A job strategy that defines variables with lists of values and runs the job once for each combination.
example: Three versions on two systems gives six jobs.

simple_definition: A compact way to write repeating times.
technical_definition: A five-field notation (minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week) with the operators *, comma, hyphen and slash that describes when a scheduled task runs.

simple_definition: A workflow that other workflows can call as a whole.
technical_definition: A workflow whose on key includes workflow_call, so that a job in another workflow can run it using the uses keyword, passing inputs and secrets.

simple_definition: A named deployment target with its own rules and secrets.
technical_definition: A named target such as staging or production, configured with protection rules, secrets and variables, that a workflow job can reference.

simple_definition: A machine you run yourself to do the jobs of a workflow.
technical_definition: A machine deployed and maintained by the user that executes GitHub Actions jobs instead of a machine provided by the platform.
example: A server in your own office.

simple_definition: A name that lets only one run at a time use a shared resource.
technical_definition: A label under which the platform allows at most one workflow run or job to be running, with later runs waiting or earlier ones cancelled.

simple_definition: Someone else's text becoming part of your script and being run.
technical_definition: An attack in which untrusted input is substituted into the text of a script so that it is interpreted as commands.
example: A pull request title that closes a quotation and adds a command.

simple_definition: A way for a workflow to get a short-lived cloud credential instead of storing a long-lived secret.
technical_definition: OpenID Connect: the workflow requests a short-lived access token from a cloud provider that trusts GitHub.
example: A deployment job that receives a token valid for one job.

simple_definition: A simple pass/fail label that a service attaches to a commit.
technical_definition: A state (such as success or failure) with a context name that an external service sets on a commit through GitHub's API.
example: An external build reporting success on the latest commit of a pull request.

simple_definition: A detailed result of an automated job, shown on a pull request.
technical_definition: A check run created by a GitHub App, including GitHub Actions, with output, annotations and messages.
example: The Checks tab of a pull request.

simple_definition: A list of the packages your project depends on.
technical_definition: GitHub's map of a repository's dependencies built from manifests and lock files.
example: Packages listed in a manifest file.

simple_definition: GitHub's helper that warns about vulnerable dependencies and opens pull requests to update them.
technical_definition: A set of features: alerts, security updates and version updates.
example: A pull request that raises a package to a fixed version.

simple_definition: A block that stops a push containing a secret.
technical_definition: A secret scanning feature that rejects pushes with detected secrets before they reach the repository.
example: A refused push with a message naming the secret type.

simple_definition: Automatic analysis of your code for weaknesses.
technical_definition: A GitHub feature that runs analysis tools such as CodeQL and shows alerts.
example: An alert on a pull request.

simple_definition: GitHub's code analysis engine.
technical_definition: The analysis product maintained by GitHub that code scanning can use.
example: A CodeQL alert for a possible injection.

simple_definition: A published notice about a vulnerability and its fix.
technical_definition: A report describing a vulnerability, affected versions and fixed versions, drafted privately and then published.
example: An advisory with a CVE number.

simple_definition: A public identification number for a known vulnerability.
technical_definition: Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures identifier assigned by a numbering authority.
example: An advisory that carries a CVE number.

simple_definition: A file that lists the packages a project needs.
technical_definition: A dependency definition file read by package managers and by GitHub's dependency graph.
example: A file that names packages and version ranges.

simple_definition: A file that records the exact versions chosen.
technical_definition: A file generated by a package manager pinning resolved versions.
example: A file that fixes each package to one version.

simple_definition: A short fingerprint of a file that changes if the file changes.
technical_definition: A value computed from a file's bytes with a hash function such as SHA-256, used to detect change.
example: A 64-character SHA-256 value next to a download.

simple_definition: A signed statement about where and how a file was built.
technical_definition: A signed record, for example made with Sigstore, linking an artifact to its source and build instructions.

simple_definition: Everything your software is made from and built with.
technical_definition: The code, dependencies, tools, build systems and people involved in producing software.
example: A dependency that an attacker changes.

simple_definition: Software whose code is public and whose licence lets others use, change and share it.
technical_definition: Software distributed under a licence that grants permissions to use, study, modify and redistribute the source.
example: A library with a licence file that permits reuse.

simple_definition: A person who looks after a project and decides what is merged.
technical_definition: A person who reviews and merges changes, triages issues and manages releases of a project.
example: The person who approves a pull request.

simple_definition: A person who sends a change or report to a project.
technical_definition: Someone who provides code, documentation, reports or other work to a project.
example: A stranger who fixes a typo through a pull request.

simple_definition: A written set of rules for how people behave in a project.
technical_definition: A document that defines standards of engagement in a community and procedures for problems.

simple_definition: A line in a commit message saying the author has the right to submit the change.
technical_definition: A Signed-off-by trailer added with git commit -s; it is text, not a cryptographic signature.

simple_definition: The legal right of a creator over their work.
technical_definition: A legal right, differing by country, that lets the creator control copying, distribution and adaptation of a work.
example: The author of a program holds the copyright unless they transfer it.

simple_definition: A written permission that says what others may do with a work.
technical_definition: A document in which the rights holder grants permissions, subject to conditions and with stated limitations.
example: A LICENSE file in the root of a repository.

simple_definition: A licence that asks only for credit and notices.
technical_definition: A licence whose main condition is preserving copyright and licence notices; derived works may use other terms.

simple_definition: A licence rule that what you build from the code must be shared under the same licence.
technical_definition: A licence condition requiring that distributed derivative works be licensed under the same or a compatible licence, with reach that varies (weak or strong).

simple_definition: A short standard name for a licence.
technical_definition: A short identifier from the SPDX licence list, such as MIT or Apache-2.0.

simple_definition: A family of licences for text, pictures and other non-software work.
technical_definition: Public licences built from elements such as Attribution, ShareAlike and NonCommercial.

simple_definition: A named, downloadable version of a project on GitHub.
technical_definition: A GitHub page built on a Git tag, with a title, notes and attached files.
example: Release v1.2.0 with a zip file and a notes page.

simple_definition: A description of what changed in a release.
technical_definition: Text attached to a release, written by hand or generated from merged pull requests.
example: A list of merged pull requests and contributors.

simple_definition: A file attached to a release.
technical_definition: A file uploaded to a GitHub release, in addition to the automatic source archives.

simple_definition: A zip or tar file of the files at a tag, without history.
technical_definition: An archive of a tagged commit's tree, made by GitHub for each release or locally with git archive.

simple_definition: A release marked as not yet final.
technical_definition: A release flagged as a pre-release, for example a beta.

simple_definition: A shared GitHub account that a group of people use to own repositories together.
technical_definition: An account type that can own repositories, packages and projects; people access it through their own user accounts and hold roles in it.
example: A company account with several teams.

simple_definition: An account that manages policy and billing for many organizations.
technical_definition: An account type that centrally manages multiple organizations; it does not directly own repositories.
example: A large company with many organizations.

simple_definition: A user account made for automation instead of a person.
technical_definition: A user account created to automate activity, such as continuous integration.
example: An account a build system uses.

simple_definition: Someone who is not a member of an organization but has access to some of its repositories.
technical_definition: A person given access to specific repositories of an organization without being a member.

simple_definition: The lowest level of access every member of an organization has to its repositories.
technical_definition: An organization-wide default repository permission for members; it does not apply to outside collaborators.

simple_definition: A named group of people in an organization that shares access and mentions.
technical_definition: A group of organization members used to grant repository access and to mention people together; teams can be nested.

simple_definition: A website made of files that are sent to the browser exactly as they are.
technical_definition: A site consisting of HTML, CSS and JavaScript files served without server-side code generating each page.
example: A bakery page with a few HTML files.

simple_definition: GitHub's service for publishing a static website from a repository.
technical_definition: A static site hosting service that takes files from a repository, optionally builds them, and publishes a website.

simple_definition: A domain name with nothing in front of it, like example.com.
technical_definition: A domain without a subdomain, also called a bare or root domain.

simple_definition: An HTTPS page that loads some of its parts over plain HTTP.
technical_definition: Assets such as images, style sheets or scripts referenced with http:// from a page served over HTTPS.
example: An image with a src that begins http://

simple_definition: A development environment that runs in the cloud and that you use through a browser or an editor.
technical_definition: A GitHub-hosted development environment in a Docker container on a virtual machine, created from a repository.
example: A codespace for the wordcount repository.

simple_definition: A container set up with the tools a project needs.
technical_definition: A Docker container configured for development, described by devcontainer.json in a .devcontainer folder.

simple_definition: An isolated, packaged environment that runs on a host computer.
technical_definition: An isolated runtime environment with its own filesystem and tools, started from an image.
example: A Python environment in a container.

simple_definition: A popular tool for building and running containers.
technical_definition: A platform for building container images and running containers.

simple_definition: A text file with instructions for building a container image.
technical_definition: A text file of instructions such as FROM, COPY and RUN that create a Docker image.
example: FROM an existing image, then RUN an install command.

simple_definition: Software prepared so that a tool can install it.
technical_definition: A versioned, packaged unit of software distributed through a registry and installed by a package manager.

simple_definition: A place that stores packages for download.
technical_definition: A service that hosts packages and serves them to package managers.

simple_definition: A packaged program together with everything it needs to run.
technical_definition: A stored, layered file system and configuration from which containers are started.
example: An image in the container registry.

simple_definition: Putting a version of your software where its users can use it.
technical_definition: The process of releasing a build to an environment where it runs, such as a server or a hosting platform.
example: Copying a new site version to a web host.

simple_definition: Deploying every change that passes the checks, automatically.
technical_definition: A practice in which each change that passes automated checks is deployed to production without a manual step.
example: A merge to main that goes live after the tests pass.

simple_definition: Going back to the previous working version.
technical_definition: Restoring the previously deployed version after a failed or faulty deployment.
example: Pointing the current link back at the old release folder.

simple_definition: A practice copy of production where you deploy first.
technical_definition: An environment that mirrors production and is used to check a release before it goes live.
example: A staging site that the team can test.

simple_definition: A file that points to another file or folder.
technical_definition: A file-system entry that names another path; reading through it reads the target.

simple_definition: A command-line program, gh, for working with GitHub.
technical_definition: GitHub's official command-line tool for pull requests, issues, releases, workflow runs, codespaces and more.

simple_definition: Usage information a program sends back to its maker.
technical_definition: Data about how software is used, collected and sent by the software, which may be inspected or disabled where the software allows.
example: GH_TELEMETRY=log prints what gh would send.

simple_definition: A way for one program to ask another to do something.
technical_definition: An application programming interface: a defined set of requests and responses that programs use to communicate.
example: A script asking GitHub for a repository's issues.

simple_definition: A style of API where each kind of thing has an address and you ask with HTTP requests.
technical_definition: An API style organised by resources addressed with URLs and HTTP methods, returning structured responses.

simple_definition: An API where you send a query that names exactly the fields you want.
technical_definition: A query language for APIs served at one endpoint that returns the requested structure.
example: A query that asks for the logins of your followers.

simple_definition: A message GitHub sends to your web address when something happens.
technical_definition: An HTTP request with event data that a service sends to a URL you registered when an event you subscribed to occurs.
example: A push triggering a request to your server.

simple_definition: A fingerprint that only someone with a secret key can produce.
technical_definition: A keyed hash message authentication code, here HMAC-SHA-256, used to check that a message is genuine and unaltered.
example: The X-Hub-Signature-256 header of a webhook delivery.

simple_definition: A cap on how many requests you may make in a period.
technical_definition: A limit on API requests within a time window, reported in response headers.

simple_definition: An integration with its own limited permissions that acts on GitHub.
technical_definition: An integration that uses fine-grained permissions and short-lived tokens and is not tied to a user account.
example: An app that comments on pull requests.

simple_definition: An integration that acts with the permissions a user gives it.
technical_definition: An app that a user authorises to act on GitHub within granted scopes; generally less preferred than a GitHub App.
example: A third-party tool you sign in to with GitHub.

simple_definition: Splitting a long list of results into pages.
technical_definition: Returning results in subsets with links (the Link header) to further pages.

simple_definition: GitHub's way of supporting open-source maintainers with money.
technical_definition: A GitHub program through which people and organisations sponsor maintainers, with additional terms and regional eligibility for those who receive funds.
example: A sponsor button on a repository.

simple_definition: A label with a value that you attach to repositories in an organisation.
technical_definition: Organisation-defined metadata on repositories that can be used, for example, to target rulesets.

simple_definition: The written rules by which a group runs a project.
technical_definition: The decisions, roles and rules of a project or organisation, expressed on GitHub through permissions, rulesets, code owners and community files.
example: A CONTRIBUTING file and a ruleset.
